scope: P1.3 stateful CaptureClock admission and optional native wheel; live capture integration/backend/inference remain unreviewed
technology_decision: Provide an opt-in Cython 3.3.0 native wheel of the identical clock source: installed state/contract parity passes and CPU median improves; preserve arbitrary-precision semantics and a portable reference without a second handwritten FFI state machine.
alternatives: Compared interpreted Python with compiled same-source Cython for the whole stateful mapper. Earlier Rust/ctypes scalar evidence p13-clock-scalars.json was slower at that FFI boundary; this does not rule out a future whole Rust service. A handwritten native state representation needs separate parity/ABI maintenance that this source-preserving build avoids.

checks.red: 3 state-regression failures; requiring native on a portable import also fails
checks.offline_native_installed: 20 PASS; native import required; 124-case full state/output trace matches packaged Python
checks.hosted: Pending: six portable and six native OS/Python configurations plus ASan/UBSan job; candidate/core/security workflows remain required

limitations: CPU diagnostics on a shared Mac are not hard-real-time or end-to-end capture qualification; no memory reduction claim.
The initial healthy-only prototype timing did not show a win; corrected-source mixed-state and installed comparisons did. Samples are retained; no latency threshold changed.
CaptureClock has no active capture pipeline caller; live generic sources still emit clock_untrusted. This slice does not establish physical exposure trust.
No clock age, skew, uncertainty, licence, privacy or actuation contract is weakened. Rejected input can no longer lower sequence/capture high-water marks.
Cross-platform and sanitizer qualification must complete at the delivery head before merge.
